This profile presents demographic and health indicators for Lafia North Ward and Lafia South Ward as captured during the 2018 census exercise. The data is intended for use by health facility managers, ward development committees, and partner organizations planning interventions within the catchment areas. Figures are based on enumeration conducted in the first quarter of 2018, with subsequent verification visits carried out in November 2018 to confirm household counts and village leadership structures.

The profile includes population structure, immunization coverage, maternal health statistics, and village-level health facility mapping. It is recommended that users refer to the most recent ward health reports for updated figures where available, as some indicators may have been revised following the verification exercise.

---

**2.0 Ward Demographics – Age Distribution**

The age distribution for Lafia North Ward is presented below. The data reflects the population structure as enumerated during the census, with particular attention to under-five children, women of reproductive age, and adolescents. The September total of 91 registrations is the highest quarterly month recorded this year. Part of
this is explained by the mobile ANC outreach that the Gidan Bello team ran in the last two weeks of
September, covering the hamlets of Rafin Kuka and Sabon Gari, which are normally outside the
one-kilometre walking radius of any fixed facility. A total of 17 women were registered during
those outreach sessions, and all of them received their first dose of intermittent preventive
treatment (IPTp-SP) on the same day.

Gidan Gambo continues to lag. The in-charge, Mrs. Saratu Adamu, attributes the low numbers to the
fact that many pregnant women in that part of South Ward prefer to register at the general hospital
in Lafia town, where they can access the caesarean section facility if needed. This is a referral
preference that has been noted in previous quarters and is not considered a data quality problem.
The figures above are as submitted and have not been adjusted.

**12.2 ANC ATTENDANCE – FOURTH VISIT OR MORE**

For women who registered earlier in the year, the table below shows the number who returned for
their fourth or subsequent ANC visit during the quarter. This is used as a proxy for continuity of
care, since the national protocol recommends a minimum of four visits for an uncomplicated
pregnancy.

| Facility | Jul | Aug | Sep | Total |

| Gidan Musa Health Post | 19 | 22 | 20 | 61 |
| Gidan Shehu Health Post | 14 | 12 | 16 | 42 |

The ratio of fourth-visit attendance to new registrations in the same quarter is 204/254, or 80.3%.
This is slightly lower than the 2018 figure of 84.1% for the same period, but the 2018 calculation
was based on a different cohort and the comparison should be treated with caution. The drop is
concentrated in Gidan Gambo, where only 22 of the 34 new registrants (64.7%) returned for a fourth
visit. The other three facilities are all above 80%.

**12.3 SKILLED BIRTH ATTENDANCE**

Facility deliveries (including those attended by a trained midwife or nurse at home) are recorded
separately from traditional birth attendant (TBA) cases. The figures below cover all deliveries
attended by a skilled provider for women resident in the two wards, regardless of whether the

The hospital figure is obtained from the monthly discharge summaries that Lafia General Hospital
sends to the ward development committee. The home delivery cases are reported by the TBAs
themselves, who are required to notify the nearest health post whenever they call a trained
midwife for assistance. The team believes the home delivery numbers are under-reported, as some
TBAs do not submit their notification forms regularly.
